Excerpted from the 682 termination log:

Termination Test Record: Testing denied by O5-█.

Note: "SCP-239 knowing about SCP-682 might pose the threat of allowing her to control SCP-682, recreate its regenerative immortality and|or adaptive capabilties, or worse, 682 overriding reality itself to resist 239. We do not know what could happen so we should keep it that way. Denied."-O5-█

Notice: Test conducted prior to Incident 239-B, after which SCP-239 was placed into comatose state indefinitely.

According to this, the Foundation thinks it is too much of a risk to expose 239 to 682's qualities, and even if they were to accept the testing request, 239 is already in an indefinite coma.

item.title: Re: 682 Destruction Collective Thread
item.content:encoded:
Got a cute little theory as to why he just won’t die.

+ show block
– hide block

A thought occurred to me after reading about his interaction with 343, supposedly God himself. Assuming he is who he claims, supposedly he can’t kill it because he apparently wasn’t the one who created the gecko. And right then, something clicked. It reminded me of a concept I wrote WAY back when. There’s really only one thing in the fictional world that’s higher than God: the writer.

As long as 682 exists as a concept of the Foundationverse, it will never die in any acceptable SCP canon because he was written to be that way. The only ones who can potentially kill it off by deleting the 682 article are the site staff and the one who initially wrote the article. And as you can imagine, they won’t, not an SCP that has become so iconic and pivotal in the fiction. SCP 738 said it best: SCP literally cannot afford to get rid of one of its most popular creations.

It’s all one giant meta reference, and perhaps it’s best that way.

As for what to do in the meantime, simply do the next best thing and find a better means of getting the lizard out of arm’s reach of us. As long as the method used isn’t specifically design to kill or harm, 682 cannot adapt, at least to my knowledge.

Our best bet would be to find a way to portal him to a distant uninhabited planet in some far flung galaxy that we’ll never reach (or just quarantine said planet). I cannot express the importance of the location being uninhabited by any life, from earth or otherwise. We saw how 682 was sent to an alternate dimension and the inhabitants spat him right back out into ours again.

Option 2: pull an Aku and send him hurtling into the far flung future, perhaps to a time after humans are long gone. Good luck getting back to the past, Samurai Jack.

Side note: Dr. Jack Bright is forbidden from referring to himself as “Samurai Jack”, and may not attempt to “get back to the past” for any reason, even especially if the purpose of said attempt is the termination of SCP-682.
